name: Jade Green
lede: Jade green is a green named for the stone, and Paterson's definition spans blue-green to yellowish green.

sections.title: A name with a range
sections.body:
Paterson defines plain jade as a green in various shades, mainly yellowish-green, and jade green as a blue-green or a yellowy green [1]. Those two definitions point in opposite directions, so the name is not tied to one spot on the wheel [1]. Paterson's index lists both jade and jade green among the greens [2]. In the dictionary, then, jade green is a color word first and a stone's name second, and its range stays wide [1][2].

The nearest named neighbors are [[jade]], [[sea-green]] and [[emerald-green]], which the library places close by [3]. The stone is itself a named gem in ColorHub [3].

sections.title: Caledon Jade Green
sections.body: One precise use is in dyes. Paterson records Caledon Jade Green as a synthetic green dye discovered in 1920 [4]. "Caledon" is a dye brand name in that entry [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The books give little beyond this. We found no usable archive measurements for the name, so there is no painting data to quote [3]. The swatch is one screen reading of the name [3].
